messages.author: f58baaed192b8072
messages.subject: Missing data binary response
parts: I've worked through the approach in the manual to handle missing data in Stan. It seems relatively straightforward if the response variable is continuous. Yet,say I am estimating a logistic regression model and I have missing data for y. If y[miss] is declared in the parameters block, and I attempt to model y[miss] distributed bernoulli_logit(theta) stan issues an error. Any thoughts on how I might deal with this? Missing categorical data are quite common, so I suspect the answer applies to other settings (eg, irt with some item responses unobserved). Thanks

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Missing data binary response
parts:
On Thursday, August 27, 2015 at 3:08:25 PM UTC-4, Jackson King wrote:
I've worked through the approach in the manual to handle missing data in Stan. It seems relatively straightforward if the response variable is continuous. Yet,say I am estimating a logistic regression model and I have missing data for y. If y[miss] is declared in the parameters block, and I attempt to model y[miss] distributed bernoulli_logit(theta) stan issues an error. Any thoughts on how I might deal with this? Missing categorical data are quite common, so I suspect the answer applies to other settings (eg, irt with some item responses unobserved). Thanks

It is tedious in Stan. You can either marginalize over the missing outcomes or introduce latent variables that are positive if the outcome is 1, negative if the outcome is 0, and of undetermined sign if the outcome is missing.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Missing data binary response
parts:
On Thursday, August 27, 2015 at 4:36:29 PM UTC-4, Jackson King wrote:
Thanks. By chance, is there any code available that would help with this? I think it makes most sense to use the former, but I'm uncertain how to implement this in practice. Thanks a lot. I appreciate it

Search for log_mix in the reference manual. This requires theta = Pr(y = 1 | x), lp1 = log-likelihood assuming the missing outcome is 1, and lp2 = log-likelihood assuming the missing outcome is 0.

Ben
